editorial:
Imagine your life is picture-perfect until your wife is suddenly arrested for a murder she swears she didn't commit. That's the nightmare John Brennan faces in this gripping thriller. Russell Crowe plays John, an ordinary college teacher who refuses to give up on his wife Lara, played by Elizabeth Banks. Three years into her sentence, with their final appeal rejected and Lara losing hope, John makes a desperate choice: he'll break her out of prison himself. The movie blends family drama with a tense escape plan, keeping you invested in whether love and determination can beat the system.

The pacing builds slowly at first, then ramps up into a nail-biting final act. Crowe delivers a grounded, believable performance, and the action feels realistic rather than over-the-top. On the downside, the middle section drags a bit, and some plot details require you to just go with it. Still, if you enjoy emotional thrillers with a strong family core, this one delivers. endingExplained: John pulls off the prison break and escapes with Lara and their son to Venezuela. Along the way, he uncovers clues suggesting Lara may actually have committed the murder, including details about a fight and a missing button. Rather than confronting her, he chooses to stay by her side. The film ends with the family starting fresh abroad, leaving Lara's true guilt deliberately ambiguous.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional thrillers with a strong family core
